A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DriveX by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision and relocation of material.

before.justification: V1 reports original Waymo experiments, reconstruction of Vista-generated videos, a real nuScenes comparison, and component ablations.

after.justification: V2 reports original Waymo and PandaSet experiments, generated-video reconstruction, component ablations, and qualitative robustness and failure analyses.

M1.justification: V2 adds driving-domain fine-tuning with edge-aware inpainting masks and colored-LiDAR conditioning accumulated from adjacent frames (Sections 3.3–3.4). This extends v1's use of ViewCrafter and is distinct from the LiDAR depth supervision already present in v1. V2 also removes the need for the earlier foreground-vehicle downweighting. The iterative Gaussian optimization and unreliability-mask framework remain.

E1.justification: V2 adds PandaSet evaluation and aggressive viewpoints involving a 6 m lateral shift or a camera elevated 3 m with 30-degree pitch (Appendices F–G). V1's real nuScenes evaluation and acceleration/deceleration comparisons disappear. Waymo and reconstruction of Vista-generated videos remain; the latter is relocated to Appendix E.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds evaluated comparisons with ReconDreamer and FreeVS alongside DriveDreamer4D. V1's Appendix Table 9 comparison against MagicDrive-t and Vista is removed, although Vista remains the source of generated videos in another experiment. EmerNeRF, S3Gaussian, PVG, and StreetGaussian remain in the main Waymo comparison.

E3.justification: Reported Waymo evaluation changes from 12 to 18 selected sequences and from 640×920 to 640×960 images. V2 adds recorded-trajectory PSNR/SSIM evaluation with every fifth frame held out. Refinement intervals change from 2,000 to 3,000 steps and sampled shifts from 2–4 m to 2–6 m. It also introduces diffusion fine-tuning and revises the generative-baseline comparison protocol. Aggressive viewpoints are explicitly included during optimization.

E4.justification: V2 adds LiDAR-conditioning and fine-tuning ablations (Table 5), a qualitative fine-tuning comparison, aggressive-view tests, an unseen-vehicle-surface failure case, and mask evolution across iterations. Existing mask, buffer, noise-strength, Gaussian-model, progressive-shift, and warping analyses are retained with revisions or relocation. V1's generated-video pose-refinement and depth-prior ablations are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. V2's random training-mask sampling and changed sequence averages do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main Waymo and many ablation values change substantially. For example, DriveX's 3 m IoU/AP/FID changes from 0.1755/0.5427/95.60 to 0.2699/0.5712/79.78, under revised method and evaluation settings rather than an isolated same-setting comparison. V2 adds comparator, recorded-view, and PandaSet results while removing earlier result sets. The generated-video FID entries are unchanged between v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 9. V2 Table 2 also shows FreeVS slightly ahead on 3 m lane IoU.

T1.justification: V1's explicit measurement model V' = f(V) + epsilon and its distortion/noise formulation (Equation 3) are omitted in v2's restoration formulation. The Gaussian rendering, photometric loss, trajectory, warping, and mask mathematics are otherwise largely retained or renumbered. Neither version contains theorem or proof developments.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list redefine the methodological novelty around inpainting that separates degradation identification from generation and avoids simulating specific degradation patterns during training. V1 foregrounded a generic inverse-problem formulation and AI-generated driving worlds. The generated-world application remains in v2's appendix but is no longer a headline contribution. The central free-form synthesis objective remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations for LiDAR guidance, domain-specific texture improvement, the training/inference mask gap, and expanding reliable regions during optimization. Appendices A and G discuss limitations of fixed trajectory sampling and failure on completely unseen surfaces. It also interprets slightly lower recorded-view metrics as perceptually negligible. V1's interpretation of its direct video-world-model comparison disappears with that experiment.

D1.justification: V2 specifies edge-mask construction, LiDAR accumulation and motion alignment, fine-tuning for 15,000 iterations with batch size 24 on eight RTX A6000 GPUs, full Waymo segment identifiers, the two ablation segments, and the Faster R-CNN evaluator. Conversely, v1's nuScenes initialization-image list and explicit 50% generated-data mixture are omitted. These omissions do not establish underlying procedural changes. The project address remains equivalent.

R1.justification: V2 substantially updates positioning through FreeSim, Difix3D+, StreetCrafter, ReconDreamer, and FreeVS. It contrasts its inpainting formulation with approaches requiring degradation-specific training or LiDAR-guided restoration. Earlier inverse-problem references are removed, and the novelty argument shifts toward training a driving-domain generative prior without simulating off-trajectory degradations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten. V2 separates novel-view regularization, inpainting restoration, and generative-model training into dedicated subsections. Generated-video material moves from the main method/results sections to Appendix E, and the supplementary material is reorganized into Appendices A–G. The title also adds DriveX and changes scene synthesis to view synthesis.

P2.justification: V2 expands Table 1 with recorded-view metrics, restructures Table 2 into different comparison panels, and adds a component-ablation table. Qualitative comparison grids are reorganized, and new figures cover fine-tuning, PandaSet, aggressive viewpoints, failure cases, and mask evolution. The generated-video figure and table are relocated rather than newly added, while the existing mask/refinement illustration gains clearer annotations.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the explanation and validation of the central generative mechanism through explicit training details and component tests. Recorded-view fidelity checks, more relevant generative comparators, PandaSet evaluation, and documented failure boundaries address important gaps in v1's evidence and qualification of applicability. These benefits outweigh the loss of the real nuScenes comparison, some ablations, and reproducibility details. Some claims remain too broad: Table 2 does not show uniform superiority over FreeVS. The improvement rests on stronger explanation and assessment, rather than treating changed-protocol scores as direct performance gains.
